facts.fact: Tom Allen offered to fight Mike McCoole at any time for any amount and put $500 on the counter as a forfeit, but McCoole did not respond.
Tom Allen and Mike McCoole signed articles in May 1873 for a London prize ring fight, with deposits posted through the summer and the fight set for 23 September 1873.
facts.conflict: stake: $2.40 a side as printed (465.c35, likely garbled) vs $500 a side deposits (454.c1, 457.c1)

facts.fact: Tom Allen and Ben Hogan signed articles on 25 September 1873 for a fight under the new London prize ring rules.
facts.conflict: stake: $1,000 a side (473.c2) vs $2,000 win or lose (461.c1); Hogan wanted it near Pittsburg (489.c3)

facts.fact: In October 1873 Tom Allen challenged Joe Coburn to a fight for $500 to $5,000 and offered a forfeit.
facts.conflict: Coburn's answer: declined (180.c22, 487.c5) vs said he would fight (485.c1, 488.c5, which says he put up no money); place: anywhere (488.c4) vs halfway between St. Louis and New York (465.c37, medium) vs Canada or near New Orleans (465.c38, low) vs West Virginia or Canada (485.c1, medium); 485.c1 is dated 1874-02 but published 1873-10-17

facts.fact: On 23 and 24 October 1873 Tom Allen offered to fight any man in the world and any Irish-American, and offered a standing bet of his money and property.
On 28 and 29 November 1873 Tom Allen challenged Ben Hogan to fight in Canada within weeks, and Hogan declined for now because of illness.
facts.conflict: time limit: within ten weeks (499.c1), two days to ten weeks' notice (499.c2), within six weeks (500.c2, medium); stake: $1,000 (499.c1) vs garbled '@5 000 to $1,000' (499.c2, low)

facts.fact: In January 1874 Tom Allen challenged Jem Mace, Joe Coburn or any other man to a London prize ring fight for $1,000 to $5,000 a side.
facts.conflict: stake: $10,000 backing for any man (046.c1) vs $1,000 to $5,000 a side (049.c1, 049.c2)

facts.fact: In February 1874 Jem Mace was reported willing to accept Tom Allen's challenge, with a forfeit required.
facts.conflict: Mace's acceptance: accepted outright (048.c1, 505.c1, medium) vs conditional on a deposit (048.c2, 050.c4, medium)

facts.fact: In November 1874 Tom Allen denied a New York report of a challenge to Bell's Life and said his earlier challenge had never been accepted.
facts.conflict: Mace's response: a New York telegram said Mace had accepted and would enter the ring next May (511.c1, medium) vs Allen offered and Mace, Coburn or others 'said nothing' (511.c4)

facts.fact: A further Allen–Hogan fight was set for 18 or 19 November 1873, near Omaha or in Canada, with the stakes raised to $2,500.
